source.title: Camera traps and deep learning enable efficient large-scale density estimation of wildlife in temperate forest ecosystems

gates.reason: independent 10-protected-area German camera-trap programme; not MICA, Snapshot Japan, or an E2-E4 derivative

public methods specify one-year deployments and daily time-lapse checks for interruptions, but the response-blind OSF file structure has not yet been inspected to prove separately retained effort fields

the same Cuddeback C2 protocol and deployment-linked ranging-pole calibration were applied across 10 geographically distinct protected areas, so the detection-calibration mechanism is not confined to one geography

at least two known-distance reference images were recorded at each camera location and used to estimate animal-to-camera distances; whether those calibration materials or their deployment linkage are retained in the public OSF package remains unopened
586 cameras across 10 protected areas provide ample public-design capacity; exact training/heldout geography has not been selected
the common field programme ran from October 2019 through September 2020, providing all 12 calendar months before any geography split is frozen
candidate-specific model freeze remains forbidden until OSF schema/effort/calibration linkage is verified response-blind

decision.next_step: freeze and execute an OSF manifest-only precheck; inspect no file contents

interpretation.supported: this is the first screened E5 candidate whose published design jointly supplies multi-geography overlap, deployment-linked distance calibration, year-round coverage, and large physical replication
not_supported: claim that the public OSF package retains the needed deployment/calibration linkage
claim that G2 or final G4 has passed
claim about any species activity pattern
